analysis.title: U.S. ETF Investors Continue to Rotate Into Defensive Strategies
key_insights: U.S. ETF flows (as a ratio of assets) into risk-on equity strategies have slowed while flows into risk-off equities and bonds have accelerated. In October 2026 the bond flows-to-assets ratio was the highest since the start of 2025.

Dividend and covered call ETFs made up two-thirds of Equity-Risk-Off ETF inflows in the trailing quarter through October 27, 2026. Dividend ETF inflows were $19.8B and covered call inflows were $15.9B.
Quality-factor ETFs took in $3.7B and Health Care ETFs took in $2.8B in the trailing three months. Both categories had outflows in 1H 2026.
SCHD was up 31.1% YTD through October 27 against 14.2% for VOO, with a 3.0% trailing-12-month yield. It took in $9.4B in three months, almost half of the dividend ETF category's inflows.

45% of covered call inflows went to ETFs that write options on the Nasdaq-100, such as JEPQ. CFRA reads this as a 'wait and watch' stance on tech: investors stay in the sector, give up some upside and take income.

Consumer Staples ETFs lost $1.1B and Telecom ETFs lost $0.4B over three months. Almost all Staples outflows came in the past month, even though the sector returned about 6%, which CFRA reads as investors selling the rally.
Non-tech risk-on ETF flows fell from a 2.9% monthly flows-to-assets ratio in January 2026 to 0.1% in October 2026, the lowest since mid-2025.

Momentum ETFs had $5.2B of outflows over three months after $7.0B of inflows in Q2 2026. Financials ETFs lost $7.5B over three months, their third straight quarter of outflows. IWM lost $2.1B. Small cap inflows slowed from a $12.0B peak in Q4 2025 to $4.1B.
Emerging markets ETFs took in $14.3B over three months, the only part of non-tech risk-on still drawing meaningful money.

Tech ETFs took in $31.8B over three months versus $74.3B in Q2 2026 alone. Monthly tech flows peaked at 1.7% of assets in June, fell to 0.06% in August and 0.34% in September, then recovered to about 1.25% in October.
New tech money is going to broader tech and growth funds. Memory chip ETFs have seen some outflows and semiconductor ETFs have had roughly flat flows over three months.

Ultra short and short-duration bond ETFs took in $82.6B over three months, 44% of all bond ETF inflows, up from $69.9B in Q1 2026 and $48.3B in Q2 2026. These funds yield 3.5%-3.8%. AAA CLO floating-rate ETFs added $8.7B.

Long-duration bond ETFs took in $13.0B over three months after flat or negative flows in each of the previous four quarters. Long Treasury funds took $10.9B of that, led by TLT. TLT is down 3.8% YTD and 7.7% over 12 months, and ZROZ is down 14% over one year.
The report says the Fed raised rates in September and held in October 2026.

Q3 hyperscaler earnings and neocloud financing conditions are the key drivers of risk appetite. Nebius reports November 10. Strong cash flow conversion and open credit markets could send money back into tech. Spending outrunning cash flow and rising borrowing costs would strengthen the move into quality, income and short-term bonds.

market_movers.rationale: CFRA flags it as a positive implication of the rotation into quality. It led quality-factor ETF inflows.

sector_views.rationale: Health Care ETFs added $2.8B in three months, a reversal from 1H 2026 outflows. CFRA says Health Care offers protection with upside potential.
Staples ETFs lost $1.1B in three months despite a roughly 6% sector return. CFRA says the sector offers stability but limited growth.
Tech is still the largest destination for risk-on flows, but flows slowed to $31.8B from $74.3B in Q2 2026. Investors are in a wait and watch mode.
Financials ETFs lost $7.5B over three months, the third straight quarter of outflows.

earnings_insights: Microsoft (MSFT) Q3 reported: beat expectations with 48% Azure growth and $18.6B of free cash flow, and its shares rose.
Alphabet (GOOGL) reported: cloud growth of 103%, a second straight quarter of negative free cash flow (-$9.1B) after more than doubling capex. Its shares fell after the earnings announcement.
Nebius (NBIS) is scheduled to report results on November 10. CFRA calls it an important signal for AI spending turning into cash flow.

macro_indicators.reading: Raised rates in September 2026, held in October 2026
macro_indicators.interpretation: Short-duration bond funds pay 3.5%-3.8% with almost no price risk, and floating-rate CLO ETFs benefit from possible further hikes.
Investors are moving toward bonds as risk-on equity flows slow.

risk_factors: Covered call ETF investors could lag the market if tech rebounds sharply.
Long-duration bond ETFs carry significant price risk and depend on timing rate cuts. CFRA says investors have lost money on TLT by mistiming cuts.
Neocloud financing stress could spread. Investors demanded yields near 15% on CoreWeave bonds carrying a 9.6% coupon.
If AI spending keeps outrunning cash flow and borrowing costs rise, defensive rotation is likely to strengthen.
vol_and_positioning: Covered call ETFs took in $15.9B over three months and 45% of that went to Nasdaq-100 option-writing funds such as JEPQ. Investors give up upside in exchange for income and a modest cushion.
Momentum ETFs had $5.2B of outflows over three months as investors pulled back from crowded trades.
Buffer ETFs took in $6.0B over three months, continuing consistent growth.

tension_points.bull_case: If earnings show AI spending turning into cash flow and credit markets stay open, money parked in short-term bonds and defensive equity could flow back into tech. MSFT beat with $18.6B of free cash flow and its shares rose.
tension_points.bear_case: If spending keeps outrunning cash flow and borrowing costs rise, the move into quality, income and short-term bonds is likely to strengthen. GOOGL had negative free cash flow of $9.1B and CoreWeave bonds yield nearly 15%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nebius results on November 10 showing AI spending turning into cash flow, with credit markets staying open, would reverse the defensive rotation.

theme_stances.key_argument: Flows into risk-off equities and short-duration bonds have accelerated while risk-on flows slowed.
theme_stances.evidence: investors have rotated into defensive equity and bond strategies in the last few months

theme_stances.key_argument: Tech is still the largest risk-on destination, but investors are rebuilding positions cautiously rather than chasing the rally.
theme_stances.evidence: investors are in "wait and watch" mode
